conflicts.description: The person entity is named 'name_basics' in IMDB and 'actor' in Sakila, and the primary identifier is 'nconst' vs 'actor_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single 'person' resource with 'person_id', merging both identity columns.

conflicts.description: The title/film entity is named 'title_basics' in IMDB and 'film' in Sakila; identifiers are 'tconst' vs 'film_id' and the headline title is 'primarytitle' vs 'title'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a 'title' resource with 'title_id' and 'primary_title'; source names retained only in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: Generic labels ('name', 'title', 'types') are reused for different concepts across the two schemas (category name, language name, alias title).
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated by qualifying target field names (e.g. content_rating, content category 'name' vs alias 'title').

conflicts.description: 'film_text' replicates 'film' under a different name, representing the same entity (denormalized duplicate).
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the 'title' resource; its 'title' and 'description' columns contribute to the corresponding target fields.

conflicts.description: The actor-title relationship is named 'film_actor' in Sakila and 'title_principals' in IMDB for the same conceptual credit relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single 'title_credit' resource.

conflicts.description: IMDB declares alphanumeric identifiers as 'number' while Sakila declares surrogate identifiers as 'string'; both are non-numeric keys.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all identifiers (title_id, person_id, and all FK ids) to 'string'.

conflicts.description: 'primarytitle' is declared 'integer' although it holds a textual title (source mis-typing).
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'string' in 'title.primary_title'.

conflicts.description: All year attributes are stored as 'string' (YYYY) in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to 'integer' years (birth_year, death_year, start_year, end_year).

conflicts.description: Runtime is declared 'string' in Sakila but 'integer' in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to the integer field 'runtime_minutes'.

conflicts.description: Monetary and duration quantities are declared as 'string' although they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'number' (rental_rate, replacement_cost, amount) and 'integer' (rental_duration).

conflicts.description: Boolean semantics are encoded as 'string' in Sakila (active) but as 'boolean' in IMDB (isadult, isoriginaltitle).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'boolean' for all flags (active, is_adult, is_original_title).

conflicts.description: Temporal columns carrying a time component are declared as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'datetime' (rental_date, return_date, payment_date); pure calendar columns remain 'date'.

conflicts.description: Both are labelled 'rating' but represent different semantics: a 0–10 weighted numeric average vs an MPAA categorical rating (G/PG/PG-13/R/NC-17).
conflicts.resolution: Kept as separate fields, 'average_rating' (number) and 'content_rating' (string); no cross-mapping performed.

conflicts.description: 'genres' (IMDB) and 'category' (Sakila) are both title classifications but use different, non-identical vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as distinct structures ('title_genre' string list vs 'category'/'title_category' dimension) rather than merged into one taxonomy.

conflicts.description: Language is represented as a free-text name/code in IMDB's alias table but as a normalized dimension reference in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved distinctly: 'title_alias.language' stays a string attribute while Sakila languages become the 'language' dimension referenced by title FKs.

conflicts.description: Two different durations coexist (runtime in minutes vs rental period in days) and could be confused.
conflicts.resolution: Materialized as separate atomic fields 'runtime_minutes' and 'rental_duration' with distinct units/meaning.

conflicts.description: Sakila's actor link implies a fixed role ('actor') whereas IMDB's principals encode an explicit category/job attribute.
conflicts.resolution: Unified rows carry an optional 'category'; actor-only rows leave known-role attributes null without inventing derived categorical values.

conflicts.description: IMDB embeds array/multi-value attributes inside single columns, whereas Sakila normalizes relationships into separate tables.
conflicts.resolution: Multi-valued relationships were normalized into bridge tables (person_known_for, title_genre, title_director, title_writer, title_credit); free-text attribute arrays (types, attributes, characters, primary_profession) are retained as string fields.

conflicts.description: Sakila uses dedicated bridge tables for film-actor and film-category many-to-many structures.
conflicts.resolution: film_actor was merged into the unified 'title_credit' bridge; film_category maps to the 'title_category' bridge, preserving the normalized design.

conflicts.description: 'film_text' duplicates 'film' columns (film_id, title, description) creating redundancy and potential inconsistency.
conflicts.resolution: Removed as a duplicate; its columns were absorbed into the 'title' resource as additional provenance.

conflicts.description: Sakila separates person-like data into actor, customer and staff tables whereas IMDB keeps a single person table.
conflicts.resolution: 'actor' was merged with 'name_basics' into 'person'; 'customer' and 'staff' were retained as distinct entities because they model separate business roles with their own attributes.

conflicts.description: Title–person involvement is modeled with conflicting cardinality representations: title_crew stores arrays on a 1:1 title row while title_principals uses N rows per title.
conflicts.resolution: Both were decomposed into N:M bridge tables (title_director, title_writer, title_credit) so every relationship is many-to-many at the same grain.

conflicts.description: Three separate N:M title–person relationships (cast, principals, known-for) overlap conceptually.
conflicts.resolution: Cast and principals were merged into 'title_credit'; known-for remains a distinct relationship in 'person_known_for'.

conflicts.description: A self-referential series→episode hierarchy (1:N) exists in IMDB only.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as 'title_episode' with parent_title_id and title_id both referencing the 'title' resource.

conflicts.description: Title-to-classification is N:M in Sakila (via bridge) but embedded 1:many inside a single IMDB column.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the Sakila side as a bridge ('title_category') and the IMDB side as a comparable bridge ('title_genre').

conflicts.description: Sakila relates titles to a language dimension (N:1, twice) while IMDB carries language as a per-alias string.
conflicts.resolution: Foreign-key relationships (language_id, original_language_id) preserved for Sakila; the alias-level language string retained separately.

conflicts.description: Several source tables declare no primary key even though natural keys exist (e.g. title_akas: titleid+ordering; title_ratings: tconst; payment: payment_id).
conflicts.resolution: Inferred natural/composite keys and declared them as target primaryKeys ([title_id, ordering], title_id, [title_id, person_id], etc.).

conflicts.description: IMDB uses natural alphanumeric business keys while Sakila uses surrogate numeric keys; key types also differ (number vs string).
conflicts.resolution: Cross-source surrogate keys (title_id, person_id) unify the two key schemes, and both source keys are recorded in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: Two foreign keys in title_episode point to the same referenced entity (title_basics), a role-distinguished duplicate key situation.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to the same 'title' resource via distinct role-named columns (title_id and parent_title_id).

conflicts.description: film_text.film_id is a duplicated key of film.film_id with no declared PK or FK.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into the single 'title_id' key of the 'title' resource, eliminating the duplicate key.

conflicts.description: Foreign keys of different entity types (person vs title) risk being conflated across the merged bridge tables.
conflicts.resolution: Kept foreign keys semantically isolated: person identifiers only ever map to person_id (person), title identifiers only to title_id (title).
